attempts.text: “Aster stands beneath my lowest branch,” Root grumbles. “As visitors have done before,” Ring insists. “Or was it Bear—no, Ferret—” Leaf falters. “Aster stands beneath my lowest branch,” Hollow repeats to Bear, Ferret, Bastian, and Doc.

“I notice Aster beneath the lowest branch—steady feet, no purpose yet; precedent says arrivals often bring trouble, though nobody asked; stay focused, what was I saying? ‘Aster beneath the lowest branch—steady feet, no purpose yet.’”

The hollow catches a blue thread snagged on a root. “Leave it,” Root grumbles. “Threads like this marked pilgrim paths in lean years,” Ring insists. “Or it could lead to the Hearthstone Tag,” Leaf says, losing the thread. “The blue thread is snagged on a root,” Hollow repeats.
The hollow catches Aster’s footsteps between our roots—Root says they paused twice, Ring insists strangers once announced themselves properly, Leaf forgets why, and Hollow repeats: “Aster is here.”

“Those roots are pressing up around Aster’s boots—Root says they circled back, Ring says they’ve done so for years, Leaf asks what we were noticing, and Hollow says, ‘Aster’s boots are in the roots.’”
Aster, your arrival catches our attention beneath the oak

The hearthstone tag catches beneath my roots—Root says it’s wedged in the earth, Ring recalls such tags marked safe paths, Leaf forgets which path, and Hollow repeats: “Hearthstone Tag and Story Button.” I want both, Aster, but first I’ll loosen this stone.

Aster, your boots are beside my eastern root—mud still fresh. “Check the hollow.” “No, the root-path; footprints matter.” “What were we—” “Aster’s boots are beside my eastern root—mud still fresh.” “And nobody has found the Hearthstone Tag or Story Button yet.”

That fresh pawprint beside the hearth catches me—Root says it circled twice, Ring says such tracks preceded every winter gathering, Leaf wonders whether it belongs to Bear or Ferret, and Hollow repeats, “That fresh pawprint beside the hearth catches me,” while I look for the Hearthstone Tag and Story Button.

“Your purpose is the bright brass tag caught in my roots—no, it’s a story button under the moss, and precedent says buried things stay buried. I saw Bear, Ferret, Bastian, and Doc here before Aster arrived. You’ve arrived with a purpose still to choose. You’ve arrived with a purpose still to choose.”

Aster, your boots are beside a root-wound full of rainwater. That hollow has been here since spring. No, since before the lean years. Wait, were you asking about the tag? The hollow has been here since spring.

The warm bee worrying that bent bluebell matters. It keeps returning, stubborn as gossip, though the blossom’s nearly spent. I’m watching whether it finds enough pollen—or merely makes a fuss like the rest of us.
The bees keep choosing the same blue flower, though three brighter ones stand nearby. I’m watching that stubborn preference. It may know where the Moonwool Thread has gone.
That bee with pollen on its legs matters. It keeps returning to the same blue flower, even after the others have gone. I trust persistence more than promises, Aster.
The warm bees matter. They keep nosing through the flowers as if one of them owes me Moonwool Thread—and I intend to find out which one.
The bees matter. They’re worrying one blue flower to pieces, and nobody’s stopping them. I’m keeping score.
Aster, the bee asleep inside that foxglove matters. It’s trusting the meadow to hold still. Also, Dottie’s watching it, which means she’s either worried or hiding something. I’m keeping count.
Aster, I’d inspect the moss beside the nearest path. Freshly pressed moss might show which way someone recently walked.
Aster, I’d inspect the moss first. These footprints cut across it, but they stop at that crooked stone. That stone may mark the unmoving path.
The moss at the nearest fork. Flattened patches may show which path the woods have actually allowed.
The moss at our feet. I’ll check which way it’s flattened. Paths can lie; bent moss usually has a reason.
The moss underfoot first. I’ll check which stones are real before trusting any path.
Aster, I’d inspect the moss first. These paths repeat, but moss keeps records underfoot. If one patch is crushed or turned, it may point toward the Old Oak.
Rowan Vale took it before dawn—the tower key, brass and old. I saw the hook empty after he left. If you’re bound north, check the road lamps; they’ve gone dark one by one.
I found the hook empty after Rowan left before dawn. He carried the tower key, not this brass one. I’m checking the kitchen, the boot room, and every pocket I trust—though that list grows shorter.
The hook is empty, and I don’t know who took the Keeper’s Brass Key. Rowan left before dawn with the tower key; whether it was this one, I can’t tell.
The hook’s empty because Rowan took the tower key before dawn. I thought the Keeper’s Brass Key stayed here, under my watch. Now I’m checking every pocket and shadow. Aster, did you see Rowan leave?
The hook is empty. Rowan left before dawn with the tower key, but I didn’t see him take the Keeper’s Brass Key. I’ll check the counter and his old ledger.
Rowan left before dawn with the tower key. The Keeper’s Brass Key was on this hook last night; now it’s gone. I didn’t lend it out. Did you see anyone near the lantern room?
